speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the pattern of funding from the National Productivity Fund (NPF) by industry in the past five years; (b) whether the NPF uses research to benchmark Singapore's productivity according to sectors with other developed countries and when deciding how much to fund each sector; and (c) whether NPF is also funding initiatives undertaken by trade associations and business chambers in addition to Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Projects supported by NPF complement our wider range of schemes and projects in driving productivity improvements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For example, to identify suitable interventions for greater productivity in the retail and food services sectors, productivity benchmarking studies were commissioned on industry performance and efficiency in areas such as labour and space, in Singapore and overseas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The design and implementation of projects are done in close collaboration and/or consultation with trade associations (TACs) and the Employment and Employability Institute (e2i).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Working with the relevant TACs helps ensure that initiatives are designed to meet the needs of the industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For example, the Hotel Innovation Committee (HIC), in an effort led by the Singapore Hotel Association (SHA) and supported by the Singapore Tourism Board (STB), steered the sector to adopt technology solutions to raise productivity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The HIC developed initiatives like the Hotel Technology Directory to connect industry players with technology solution providers as they sought to transform their business processes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This has helped spur the adoption of solutions such as the self-check-in technology that is integrated with STB’s E-Visitor Authentication system, robotics and RFID tracking.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The second supplementary question is, is the approach taken by the NPF more proactive or reactive, or is it a blend of both?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Meaning to say that, can any organisation pitch a project to the NPF to request funding or is it the case that the NPF is not really open to that sort of modus operandi and they will just determine what sectors or what projects they want to do in any particular year?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And thirdly, I am wondering if the NPF makes easily available online a statement of its objectives, its KPIs, its strategies, maybe a review of what it has done in the past year.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Many Statutory Boards and agencies do have their annual reports online where the CEO will talk about the agencies' priorities, what they did in the previous year, what their goals are for the coming year and so on.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I found it quite difficult to search for this information – and I stand corrected if I just did not try hard enough – and I only found some information on the NPF for 2010 and 2017.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For 2017, I was able to find the annual report; it is a very brief annual report and I found it through the National Archives website, actually.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, I was just wondering if this information is easily available and if not, will it be made easily available, going forward, given the tremendous amount of funding that is going into the NPF?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Please keep it concise and a reminder to try to keep it to two supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member Mr Leon Perera for his three questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to take a step back to recap.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Mr Leon Perera and Members would remember that the NPF was set up in 2010 to support programmes relating to productivity enhancement as well as Continuing Education and Training (CET).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It came about because of the Economic Strategies Committee (ESC).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It was part of the wider push for productivity growth arising from the ESC recommendations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The NPF has been set up since 2010, so it has been about 13 years.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The NPF, especially since the formation of the Future Economy Council, also supports the work of the 23 Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) Committee of Supply (COS) on Tuesday has highlighted the work of the ITMs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The ITMs are not just under the purview of MTI and our nine economic agencies.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Some of the other agencies and Ministries are involved.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, for the build environment, the Building Construction Authority (BCA) is very involved in spearheading the built environment ITM.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The NPF supports the work of the Future Economy Council that drives the growth and the transformation of Singapore's economy for the future.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: You would remember that for the ITMs, there are a few pillars.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Innovation, internationalisation, creating good jobs for Singaporeans today and tomorrow.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, the establishment and the top-up for the NPF highlights the Singapore Government's strong commitment towards productivity enhancement and CET.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure the Member that the productivity projects that are funded by the NPF complements the wide range of schemes and projects, not just in MTI but, like I said, across the Ministries and agencies in improving productivity of all sectors of the economy.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I gave the number for the disbursement over the last five years.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: At this juncture, let me share one number, for a sense of our overall progress in productivity improvements.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is consistent with the target growth rate of 2% to 3% set in 2010 when the NPF was set up.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The work of the ITM is such that the sector agency cannot create policies in isolation.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We have to work with the TACs because they play a very important role, advocating for the sector, bridging the communication with the sector and connecting the sector together, being a voice for the sector.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In my reply to the Parliamentary Question (PQ), you would have heard me using the example of the hotels.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: STB works closely with SHA to bring that about.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: That is really how we get buy-in to level up the productivity across the sector, sector by sector and in fact, sub-sector by sub-sector.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Whether it is the hotel, retail, food services or construction sectors, and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Member also asked whether companies can apply for NPF funding.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The companies that are interested can certainly approach the sector agencies or even the TACs that might be involved.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to share with him that the funds from the NPF are used to support meritorious productivity and CET schemes.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Each of the project will have different criteria to meet, whether it is the vertical sectoral-specific ones or the horizontal ones.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To the Member's last question to make available more information, this is certainly done across all ITMs, sharing about how we are working together with the TACs, companies in the sector and trade unions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The various trade unions are very involved in working with the TACs and the sector agencies to curate these jobs and also to implement the productivity drive.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Amongst the eight initiatives under the hotel productivity plan, one of them is to proliferate shared services at the group level.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: STB has exceeded the KPI in this initiative.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I will not bore you with the details but I will highlight how it has done so.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It embarked on more than 40 projects at group level to encourage our hotels to develop centralised systems in areas like IT, HR, property management, customer management, and also to adopt shared services such as group level branding and marketing.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And in so doing, to raise the productivity such that we can create better well-paying jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I will keep it to two and I thank you for your indulgence, Mr Speaker, Sir.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The second supplementary question is, would the Ministry commit to making available clear statements online of what the NPF activities are, what its goals are, what its priorities are, based on the research that it is doing and to make this available to the members of the public?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member for his two supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In a way, the TACs and the companies are tapping on the funding as well.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I also want to assure him that MTI economists also conduct regular studies to examine the individual impact of key schemes under NPF.
